$comment: DERIVED - not verbatim. Written by this library from the prose of OSV Schema v1.9.2 (docs/schema.md at tag v1.9.2, sha256 96d82f03d763fb408bc344d01fc271f761a81cc225f6f6a42d318e3ed21cebff). It holds only rules the prose states that neither osv.schema.json (validation/schema.json, verbatim) nor vulnerability.proto enforces. Apply it IN ADDITION to osv.schema.json: a record conforms only if it is valid against both. Each rule P01 to P12 quotes its source lines; schema/README.md lists them.
title: OSV Schema v1.9.2: prose rules that validation/schema.json does not enforce (derived)

P01-id-character-set.title: P01 id: only ASCII letters, digits and the characters : _ . -
P01-id-character-set.$comment: L154: 'the `id` field must strictly use ASCII characters matching the regular expression:'; L157: '^[a-zA-Z0-9:_.-]+$'; L160: 'Characters outside this set (such as spaces, slashes `/`, backslashes `\`, parentheses, or exclamation marks) are not allowed.'; osv.schema.json checks only the home-database prefix ($defs/prefix, not anchored at the end), so it accepts x_a b/c

P02-timestamps-utc-z.title: P02 modified, published, withdrawn: the whole value is an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC ending in Z
P02-timestamps-utc-z.$comment: L716-L717: 'The `modified` field gives the time the entry was last modified, as an RFC3339-formatted timestamp in UTC (ending in "Z").'; L734-L735: 'The `published` field gives the time the entry should be considered to have been published, as an RFC3339-formatted time stamp in UTC (ending in "Z").'; L745-L746: 'The `withdrawn` field gives the time the entry should be considered to have been withdrawn, as an RFC3339-formatted timestamp in UTC (ending in "Z").'; osv.schema.json $defs/timestamp has the same pattern without ^ and $, so when format is not asserted (the 2020-12 default) it accepts any string that contains a timestamp. This rule anchors it; calendar ranges (month 13, hour 25) still need format date-time asserted

P03-semver-range-versions.title: P03 SEMVER ranges: event versions are SemVer 2.0.0 with no leading v (introduced may be 0; limit may contain *)
P03-semver-range-versions.$comment: L1098-L1099: '`SEMVER`: The versions `introduced` and `fixed` are semantic versions as defined by [SemVer 2.0.0](https://semver.org), with no leading "v" prefix.'; L1143-L1144: 'The values of `introduced`, `fixed`, `last_affected` and `limit` are version strings as defined by the `affected[].ranges[].type` field.'; L1151-L1152: '`introduced` allows a version of the value `"0"` to represent a version that sorts before any other version.'; L1153: '`limit` allows versions containing the string `"*"` to represent "infinity".'; neither osv.schema.json nor vulnerability.proto checks SEMVER versions

P04-git-range-zero-only-introduced.title: P04 GIT ranges: only introduced may be 0; fixed, last_affected and limit are commit hashes
P04-git-range-zero-only-introduced.$comment: L1122-L1123: '`GIT`: The versions `introduced` and `fixed` are full-length Git commit hashes.'; L1143-L1144: 'The values of `introduced`, `fixed`, `last_affected` and `limit` are version strings as defined by the `affected[].ranges[].type` field.'; L1151-L1152: '`introduced` allows a version of the value `"0"` to represent a version that sorts before any other version.'; osv.schema.json applies ^(0|[a-f0-9]{40}|[a-f0-9]{64})$ to all four event types, so it admits 0 for fixed, last_affected and limit

P05-aliases-in-id-form.title: P05 aliases[]: each item is in the form of the id field (the P01 character set)
P05-aliases-in-id-form.$comment: L758-L759: 'The `aliases` field gives a list of IDs of the same vulnerability in other databases, in the form of the `id` field.'; reading: the form includes the id character set (P01); the home-database prefix list is not applied, as osv.schema.json does not apply it to aliases either

P06-purl-without-version.title: P06 affected[].package.purl: a Package URL (scheme pkg) without the @version component
P06-purl-without-version.$comment: L964-L966: 'The `purl` field is a string following the [Package URL specification](https://github.com/package-url/purl-spec) that identifies the package, without the `@version` component.'; the pattern checks the pkg: scheme and that no @ comes before the qualifiers (?) or the subpath (#); it is not a full Package URL check

P07-ecosystem-suffix-must.title: P07 ecosystems whose suffix the prose says must be present

allOf.title: P07a Alpine: suffix :v<RELEASE-NUMBER> required
allOf.$comment: L992: 'The ecosystem string must have a `:v<RELEASE-NUMBER>` suffix to scope the package to a particular Alpine release branch (the `v` prefix is required).'

allOf.title: P07b Mageia: suffix :<RELEASE-NUMBER> required
allOf.$comment: L1016: 'The ecosystem string must have a `:<RELEASE-NUMBER>` suffix to scope the package to a particular Mageia release.'

allOf.title: P07c Photon OS: suffix :<RELEASE-NUMBER> required
allOf.$comment: L1026: 'The ecosystem string must have a `:<RELEASE-NUMBER>` suffix to scope the package to a particular Photon OS release.'

allOf.title: P07d Red Hat Lightwell: suffix naming an existing OSV ecosystem required
allOf.$comment: L1030: 'The ecosystem **must** have a suffix matching an existing OSV ecosystem (e.g. `Red Hat Lightwell:Maven`) to denote what ecosystem the advisory is describing.'; reading: the suffix is one of the 52 ecosystem names of the table (L988-L1042), optionally followed by that ecosystem's own suffix

ecosystem.pattern: ^Red Hat Lightwell:(AlmaLinux|Alpaquita|Alpine|Android|Azure Linux|BellSoft Hardened Containers|Bioconductor|Bitnami|Chainguard|CleanStart|ConanCenter|CRAN|crates\.io|Debian|Docker Hardened Images|Echo|FreeBSD|GHC|GitHub Actions|Go|Hackage|Hex|Homebrew|Julia|Kubernetes|Linux|Mageia|Maven|MinimOS|npm|NuGet|opam|openEuler|openSUSE|OSS-Fuzz|Packagist|Photon OS|Pub|PyPI|Red Hat|Red Hat Lightwell|Rocky Linux|Root|RubyGems|SUSE|SwiftURL|TuxCare|Ubuntu|vcpkg|VSCode|Wolfi|WordPress)(:.+)?$

P08-ecosystem-suffix-has.title: P08 ecosystems whose string the prose says has a suffix (and its form, where stated)

allOf.title: P08a Alpaquita: has a :<RELEASE> suffix
allOf.$comment: L991: 'The ecosystem string has a `:<RELEASE>` suffix to scope the package to a particular Alpaquita Linux release.'

allOf.title: P08b Azure Linux: has a :<RELEASE> suffix, numeric
allOf.$comment: L994: 'The ecosystem string has a `:<RELEASE>` suffix to scope the package to a particular Azure Linux release. `<RELEASE>` is a numeric version.'

allOf.title: P08c BellSoft Hardened Containers: has a :<RELEASE> suffix
allOf.$comment: L995: 'The ecosystem string has a `:<RELEASE>` suffix to scope the package to a particular Hardened Containers release.'

allOf.title: P08d openEuler: has a <RELEASE> suffix
allOf.$comment: L1022: 'The ecosystem string has a `<RELEASE>` suffix, specifying a particular openEuler LTS Release.'; reading: written with the colon that osv.schema.json requires before any suffix ($defs/ecosystemWithSuffix)

allOf.title: P08e openSUSE: has a :<RELEASE> suffix
allOf.$comment: L1023: 'The ecosystem string has a `:<RELEASE>` suffix presenting the marketing name of the openSUSE distribution.'

allOf.title: P08f Red Hat: has a :<CPE> suffix
allOf.$comment: L1029: 'The ecosystem string has a `:<CPE>` suffix to scope the RPM to a specific Red Hat product stream.'

allOf.title: P08g SUSE: has a :<RELEASE> suffix
allOf.$comment: L1034: 'The ecosystem string has a `:<RELEASE>` suffix representing the marketing name of the SUSE product.'

allOf.title: P08h Ubuntu: :[Pro:]YY.MM[:LTS]
allOf.$comment: L1037: 'The ecosystem string has a `:<RELEASE>` suffix to scope the package to a particular Ubuntu release. `<RELEASE>` is a numeric ("YY.MM") version as specified in [Ubuntu Releases](https://wiki.ubuntu.com/Releases), with a mandatory `:LTS` suffix if the release is marked as LTS. The release version may also be prefixed with `:Pro:` to denote Ubuntu Pro (aka Expanded Security Maintenance (ESM)) updates.'

P09-ecosystem-suffix-forms.title: P09 other suffix forms the prose states (numeric release, closed lists, none, no trailing slash)

allOf.title: P09a AlmaLinux: optional suffix is a numeric version
allOf.$comment: L990: 'The ecosystem string might optionally have a `:<RELEASE>` suffix to scope the package to a particular AlmaLinux release. `<RELEASE>` is a numeric version.'

allOf.title: P09b Rocky Linux: optional suffix is a numeric version
allOf.$comment: L1031: 'The ecosystem string might optionally have a `:<RELEASE>` suffix to scope the package to a particular Rocky Linux release. `<RELEASE>` is a numeric version.'

allOf.title: P09c TuxCare: optional suffix is a numeric version
allOf.$comment: L1036: 'The ecosystem string might optionally have a `:<RELEASE>` suffix to scope the package to a particular TuxCare release. `<RELEASE>` is a numeric version.'

allOf.title: P09d Echo: suffix only PyPI, Maven, npm or NuGet
allOf.$comment: L1005: 'The supported values are `Echo:PyPI`, `Echo:Maven`, `Echo:npm` and `Echo:NuGet`.'

allOf.title: P09e WordPress: suffix only :Core, :Plugin or :Theme
allOf.$comment: L1041: 'The ecosystem string may have a suffix to specify the component: `:Core` for WordPress Core (the `name` is `wordpress`), `:Plugin` for plugins (the `name` is the plugin slug), or `:Theme` for themes (the `name` is the theme slug).'; reading: the three listed suffixes are the only ones

allOf.title: P09f vcpkg: no suffix
allOf.$comment: L1038: 'The ecosystem string has no release suffix.'

allOf.title: P09g Maven: remote repository URL suffix without a trailing slash
allOf.$comment: L1017: 'The ecosystem string might optionally have a `:<REMOTE-REPO-URL>` suffix to denote the remote repository URL that best represents the source of truth for this package, without a trailing slash (e.g. `Maven:https://maven.google.com`).'

allOf.title: P09h Packagist: remote repository URL suffix without a trailing slash
allOf.$comment: L1025: 'The ecosystem string might optionally have a `:<REMOTE-REPO-URL>` suffix to denote the remote repository URL that best represents the source of truth for this package, without a trailing slash (e.g. `Packagist:https://packages.drupal.org/8`).'

allOf.title: P09i VSCode: remote repository URL suffix without a trailing slash
allOf.$comment: L1039: 'The ecosystem string might optionally have a `:<REMOTE-REPO-URL>` suffix to denote the remote repository URL that best represents the source of truth for this package, without a trailing slash (e.g. `VSCode:https://open-vsx.org`).'

P10-package-name-forms.title: P10 package name forms the prose states for an ecosystem
P10-package-name-forms.$comment: L959-L960: 'Use the wildcard package name `*` to indicate that an advisory affects all packages within the specified `ecosystem`.'; so every name form below exempts the name *. For Linux the prose does not reconcile this with L1015 (normative.md U-24), and P10a does not decide between them

allOf.title: P10a Linux: name is Kernel
allOf.$comment: L1015: 'The only supported `name` is `Kernel`.'

allOf.title: P10b Android: a :linux_kernel: name ends in nothing or one listed SoC vendor
allOf.$comment: L993: 'One exception is when the project contains the Linux kernel source code, in which case `name` field will be `:linux_kernel:`, followed by an optional SoC vendor name e.g. `:linux_kernel:Qualcomm`.'; L2001: 'its `name` will be `:linux_kernel:`, optionally appended with one of the following SoC vendor names'; vendors from the list at L2003-L2010

allOf.title: P10c Maven: name is groupId:artifactId
allOf.$comment: L1017: 'The `name` field is a Maven package name in the format `groupId:artifactId`.'

allOf.title: P10d VSCode: name is <publisher>.<name>
allOf.$comment: L1039: 'the `name` is the `<publisher>.<name>` string which uniquely identifies a package.'

allOf.title: P10e GitHub Actions: name is {owner}/{repo}
allOf.$comment: L1008: 'the `name` field is the action's repository name with owner e.g. `{owner}/{repo}`.'

allOf.title: P10f PyPI: name is a normalized (PEP 503) package name
allOf.$comment: L1028: 'the `name` field is a [normalized](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0503/#normalized-names) PyPI package name.'; pattern: a PEP 508 project name after PEP 503 normalization (lower case; each run of . - _ replaced by one -), as the prose links it

allOf.title: P10g WordPress:Core: name is wordpress
allOf.$comment: L1041: '`:Core` for WordPress Core (the `name` is `wordpress`)'

P11-summary-one-line.title: P11 summary: one line (no line feed or carriage return)
P11-summary-one-line.$comment: L823-L824: 'The `summary` field gives a one-line, English textual summary of the vulnerability.'; English is not checked. Added in pass 3 (cross-check): pass 1 checked one-line as S02a of osv-recommended.derived.schema.json, a warning, while requirements.yaml R-0043 is a constraint and examples GAP-40 expects a two-line summary to be invalid

P12-arrays-not-null.title: P12 aliases, affected, references, severity and affected[].severity: an array, never null
P12-arrays-not-null.$comment: L758: 'The `aliases` field gives a list of IDs'; L920: 'The `affected` field is a JSON array'; L1427: 'The `references` field contains a list of JSON objects describing references.'; L851: 'The `severity` field is a JSON array'; L1069: 'The `severity` field is an optional element [defined here](#severity-field).'; osv.schema.json admits null for exactly these five (D11). Added in pass 3 (cross-check), as requirements.yaml R-0032, R-0050, R-0063 and R-0205 and examples GAP-36 to GAP-39 read them

semver-2.0.0.$comment: A SemVer 2.0.0 version (https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html, section 2, 9 and 10), no leading v; written with [0-9] rather than \d so that ECMA-262 and Python regular expressions agree
